questions.stem: Why do we group data into class intervals?

options.text: To organise data with a wide range of values into manageable groups
To make the data less accurate
To increase the number of rows in the table
To change continuous data into discrete data

questions.explanation: When data has a wide range of values, grouping into class intervals makes the data easier to read, interpret, and draw charts from.

questions.stem: A value of exactly $20.0$ is recorded. Using class intervals $10 \leq x < 20$ and $20 \leq x < 30$, which class does it belong to?

options.text: It belongs to both classes
It belongs to neither class

questions.explanation: The class $10 \leq x < 20$ does not include 20 (because of the $<$ sign). The class $20 \leq x < 30$ includes 20 (because of the $\leq$ sign).

options.text: The class with the smallest frequency
The exact mode of the data
The class interval with the highest frequency
The middle class interval

questions.explanation: The modal class is the class interval that has the highest frequency. It is the grouped equivalent of the mode.

questions.stem: What is the class width of the interval $15 \leq x < 25$?
Which of these is a problem with overlapping class intervals like $0$--$10$, $10$--$20$, $20$--$30$?

options.text: There are too many classes
A value of 10 could belong to two classes
The class widths are unequal
There are gaps between the classes

questions.explanation: With intervals $0$--$10$ and $10$--$20$, the value 10 fits in both classes. This ambiguity must be avoided by using inequality notation.

questions.stem: From a grouped frequency table with 100 items, the median lies in the class containing the:

options.text: 50th value
100th value
50th and 51st values
25th value

questions.explanation: For $n = 100$ (even), the median is the average of the $\frac{100}{2} = 50\text{th}$ and $51\text{st}$ values. You need to find which class contains these positions.

questions.stem: Why can we NOT find the exact mode from a grouped frequency table?

options.text: Because the individual data values are lost when data is grouped
Because the frequencies are too large
Because grouped data is always continuous
Because there are too many class intervals

questions.explanation: When data is grouped, we know how many values fall in each class but not the individual values. We can only identify the modal class, not the exact mode.
